title: GitHub - nicolasakf/agentize: Make your website legible to AI agents
excerpt: Make your website legible to AI agents. Contribute to nicolasakf/agentize development by creating an account on GitHub.
content_html:
Make your website legible to AI agents.

Agentize builds a semantic index of the content you choose and serves it from your own domain under /agents/*. An agent asks a question in natural language and receives your Markdown, with canonical URLs attached, instead of crawling and parsing your HTML.

Agentize is not a web crawler. It does not accept arbitrary website URLs, and it does not send your content or an agent's queries to a hosted AI provider. Embeddings are computed locally at build time. You can expose the index publicly or protect it with your company's existing authentication layer.

How it works

Suppose an agent needs to know whether your product supports enterprise single sign-on. Without a first-party interface it has to locate a likely page through a search engine or sitemap, download the HTML, strip navigation and other page chrome, and judge whether what it found is current and authoritative.

With Agentize installed, it sends one request:

curl https://example.com/agents/search \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"Can employees use a company identity provider?","limit":5}'

The response names the resource, its canonical URL, and the passages that matched the query:

{
  "results": [
    {
      "resourceId": "docs:saml",
      "url": "https://example.com/docs/saml",
      "title": "SAML single sign-on",
      "description": "Connect an enterprise identity provider.",
      "type": "documentation",
      "collection": "security",
      "updatedAt": "2026-08-20T10:00:00.000Z",
      "score": 0.93,
      "matches": [
        {
          "heading": "Supported identity providers",
          "excerpt": "Enterprise accounts can connect Okta or Entra ID...",
          "score": 0.95
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

A follow-up request to GET /agents/resources/docs:saml returns the full page as normalized Markdown. Discovery, one search, and one fetch replace a sequence of page downloads.

Quick start

Requires Node.js 22 or newer, and pnpm.

pnpm add @nicolasakf/agentize
pnpm agentize init

Declare your content sources in the generated agentize.config.ts:

import { defineConfig, markdown } from "@nicolasakf/agentize";

export default defineConfig({
  site: {
    name: "Example",
    origin: "https://example.com",
    description: "Example's authoritative agent interface",
  },
  sources: [
    markdown({ root: "content", include: ["**/*.{md,mdx}"] }),
  ],
});

Then validate, build, and serve the index:

pnpm agentize check
pnpm agentize build
pnpm agentize serve
curl http://127.0.0.1:4242/agents

The first build downloads the pinned local embedding model. Later builds reuse both the model and content-addressed embeddings, so only changed content is re-embedded.

Why a first-party index

An agent searching a website today has to reconstruct what the site knows. That works almost everywhere, and it costs several requests and most of the original structure. Agentize lets the publisher expose the same knowledge directly.

Crawling a website Asking a website
Follows links or relies on a search engine Uses a first-party interface on the publisher's domain
Parses HTML, scripts, navigation, and repeated page elements Returns normalized resources and Markdown
Often depends on exact keywords Retrieves semantically related passages while preserving exact-identifier matching
Makes the agent or search engine build the index Lets the website owner build and control the index
Infers canonical URLs, titles, types, and relationships Returns those fields explicitly
Can encounter duplicate or irrelevant routes Indexes only the sources the owner declared
Usually requires several page requests Usually needs discovery, one search, and one resource fetch
Works without cooperation from the website Requires the website owner to install and deploy Agentize

Agentize does not replace ordinary browsing. An agent can still inspect the rendered site, find content the publisher omitted, or verify claims through independent sources. An Agentize response is authoritative about what the publisher declared, not independent proof that every claim is true.

Agentize v0.2 is a proposed protocol implemented by this project, not an established web standard. Its goal is to give websites and agents a small, shared convention for first-party semantic search.

Owner-controlled sources

Markdown and MDX frontmatter can define id, route, title, description, type, collection, language, tags, updatedAt, relationships, and priority. Files marked draft: true are ignored. Files marked noindex: true are also ignored unless a protected source opts in with includeNoindex: true.

Application data is exposed explicitly:

import { defineConfig, defineResources } from "@nicolasakf/agentize";

export default defineConfig({
  site: {
    name: "Store",
    origin: "https://store.example",
    description: "The store's public catalog",
  },
  sources: [
    defineResources({
      name: "products",
      async list() {
        return database.products.findMany({ where: { published: true } });
      },
      map(product, context) {
        const route = `/products/${product.slug}`;
        return {
          id: `product:${product.id}`,
          canonicalUrl: new URL(route, context.site.origin).toString(),
          route,
          title: product.name,
          description: product.summary,
          contentMarkdown: product.description,
          type: "product",
          collection: "products",
          language: "en",
          tags: product.categories,
          relationships: [],
          priority: 0,
        };
      },
    }),
  ],
});

Dynamic framework routes require an explicit resource provider like this one. Agentize deliberately does not inspect arbitrary UI source code and guess which rendered text is authoritative.

Protected intranets

A protected Agentize interface uses one shared index for content that every admitted employee or service agent may read. The host application authenticates the complete /agents/* route family. Agentize does not manage accounts, roles, or document-level permissions.

Declare protected access and opt into intranet pages that use noindex to stay out of public search engines:

export default defineConfig({
  site: {
    name: "Example intranet",
    origin: "https://intranet.example",
    description: "Shared employee knowledge",
  },
  access: { mode: "protected" },
  sources: [
    markdown({
      root: "content/handbook",
      include: ["**/*.md"],
      includeNoindex: true,
    }),
  ],
});

Protected bundles fail closed. A framework integration must provide a host-owned request gate:

import { createAgentizeRouteHandlers } from "@nicolasakf/agentize/next";

const handlers = createAgentizeRouteHandlers({
  authorizeRequest(request) {
    return requireCompanyAccess(request);
  },
});

authorizeRequest runs before discovery, index, search, resource retrieval, and unknown Agentize paths. Return the host's 401 or 403 response to deny access, or return nothing to continue.

For a sidecar behind an authenticated reverse proxy, make the trust boundary explicit:

location ~ ^/agents(?:/|$) {
  auth_request /_company_auth;
  proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:4242;
}
agentize serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4242 --trust-upstream-protection

Use the trusted-upstream flag only when the proxy protects /agents and every path below it. Keep documents with narrower HR, finance, or team permissions out of this shared index.

Next.js

Run agentize init. It creates an App Router catch-all route under app/agents/[[...path]]/route.ts. The route uses the Node runtime because local query embedding and USearch require Node-compatible packages.

The adapter also exports withAgentize, which includes the generated bundle and native vector dependency in Next's server output:

import { withAgentize } from "@nicolasakf/agentize/next";

export default withAgentize({});

Build the Agentize bundle before the application build:

{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "agentize build && next build"
  }
}

Commands

  • agentize init creates configuration and framework integration files.
  • agentize build produces an atomic .agentize/output/ bundle.
  • agentize dev watches sources, rebuilds, and serves on port 4242. Protected bundles require --trust-upstream-protection unless the runtime receives authorizeRequest programmatically.
  • agentize serve serves a generated bundle with the same protected-mode requirement.
  • agentize check validates resources, privacy exclusions, relationships, and Next.js route coverage.

Protocol

  • GET /agents discovers the site and its agent endpoints.
  • GET /agents/index lists semantic collections and paginated standalone resources.
  • POST /agents/search performs semantic-first retrieval, with optional filters on type, collection, tag, and language.
  • GET /agents/resources/:id returns JSON, or Markdown with Accept: text/markdown.

See the v0.2 protocol for request and response shapes. The v0.1 protocol remains available for older clients.

Agent skills

This repository ships two Agent Skills for coding agents. Install them with the open skills CLI:

npx skills add nicolasakf/agentize --all

Install one skill:

npx skills add nicolasakf/agentize --skill agentize-websites
npx skills add nicolasakf/agentize --skill search-agentized-websites
Skill Use when
agentize-websites Installing, configuring, deploying, or troubleshooting Agentize in a website repository you control
search-agentized-websites Detecting and querying public or authenticated /agents/* endpoints without crawling HTML

Skills are maintained in .agents/skills/ and work with Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and 70+ other agents.

Privacy and deployment

Agentize indexes only declared sources. Admin, account, checkout, authentication, and internal API paths are excluded by default. Run agentize check in CI and review all warnings before deployment.

The generated bundle contains the full indexed text and embeddings. Treat a protected bundle as private application data and never publish it as a static asset. Protocol 0.2 targets self-hosted Node or Docker. Static and edge-only runtimes are not supported.

Every package is versioned together. Upgrading from 0.1 requires rebuilding the Agentize bundle before deployment.

Development

pnpm install
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build

content_html_zh:
Make your website legible to AI agents.

Agentize builds a semantic index of the content you choose and serves it from your own domain under /agents/*. An agent asks a question in natural language and receives your Markdown, with canonical URLs attached, instead of crawling and parsing your HTML.

Agentize is not a web crawler. It does not accept arbitrary website URLs, and it does not send your content or an agent's queries to a hosted AI provider. Embeddings are computed locally at build time. You can expose the index publicly or protect it with your company's existing authentication layer.

它是如何运作的

Suppose an agent needs to know whether your product supports enterprise single sign-on. Without a first-party interface it has to locate a likely page through a search engine or sitemap, download the HTML, strip navigation and other page chrome, and judge whether what it found is current and authoritative.

With Agentize installed, it sends one request:

curl https://example.com/agents/search \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"Can employees use a company identity provider?","limit":5}'

The response names the resource, its canonical URL, and the passages that matched the query:

{
  "results": [
    {
      "resourceId": "docs:saml",
      "url": "https://example.com/docs/saml",
      "title": "SAML single sign-on",
      "description": "Connect an enterprise identity provider.",
      "type": "documentation",
      "collection": "security",
      "updatedAt": "2026-08-20T10:00:00.000Z",
      "score": 0.93,
      "matches": [
        {
          "heading": "Supported identity providers",
          "excerpt": "Enterprise accounts can connect Okta or Entra ID...",
          "score": 0.95
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

A follow-up request to GET /agents/resources/docs:saml returns the full page as normalized Markdown. Discovery, one search, and one fetch replace a sequence of page downloads.

快速启动

Requires Node.js 22 or newer, and pnpm.

pnpm add @nicolasakf/agentize
pnpm agentize init

Declare your content sources in the generated agentize.config.ts:

import { defineConfig, markdown } from "@nicolasakf/agentize";

export default defineConfig({
  site: {
    name: "Example",
    origin: "https://example.com",
    description: "Example's authoritative agent interface",
  },
  sources: [
    markdown({ root: "content", include: ["**/*.{md,mdx}"] }),
  ],
});

Then validate, build, and serve the index:

pnpm agentize check
pnpm agentize build
pnpm agentize serve
curl http://127.0.0.1:4242/agents

The first build downloads the pinned local embedding model. Later builds reuse both the model and content-addressed embeddings, so only changed content is re-embedded.

Why a first-party index

An agent searching a website today has to reconstruct what the site knows. That works almost everywhere, and it costs several requests and most of the original structure. Agentize lets the publisher expose the same knowledge directly.

Crawling a website Asking a website
Follows links or relies on a search engine Uses a first-party interface on the publisher's domain
Parses HTML, scripts, navigation, and repeated page elements Returns normalized resources and Markdown
Often depends on exact keywords Retrieves semantically related passages while preserving exact-identifier matching
Makes the agent or search engine build the index Lets the website owner build and control the index
Infers canonical URLs, titles, types, and relationships Returns those fields explicitly
Can encounter duplicate or irrelevant routes Indexes only the sources the owner declared
Usually requires several page requests Usually needs discovery, one search, and one resource fetch
Works without cooperation from the website Requires the website owner to install and deploy Agentize

Agentize does not replace ordinary browsing. An agent can still inspect the rendered site, find content the publisher omitted, or verify claims through independent sources. An Agentize response is authoritative about what the publisher declared, not independent proof that every claim is true.

Agentize v0.2 is a proposed protocol implemented by this project, not an established web standard. Its goal is to give websites and agents a small, shared convention for first-party semantic search.

Owner-controlled sources

Markdown and MDX frontmatter can define id, route, title, description, type, collection, language, tags, updatedAt, relationships, and priority. Files marked draft: true are ignored. Files marked noindex: true are also ignored unless a protected source opts in with includeNoindex: true.

Application data is exposed explicitly:

import { defineConfig, defineResources } from "@nicolasakf/agentize";

export default defineConfig({
  site: {
    name: "Store",
    origin: "https://store.example",
    description: "The store's public catalog",
  },
  sources: [
    defineResources({
      name: "products",
      async list() {
        return database.products.findMany({ where: { published: true } });
      },
      map(product, context) {
        const route = `/products/${product.slug}`;
        return {
          id: `product:${product.id}`,
          canonicalUrl: new URL(route, context.site.origin).toString(),
          route,
          title: product.name,
          description: product.summary,
          contentMarkdown: product.description,
          type: "product",
          collection: "products",
          language: "en",
          tags: product.categories,
          relationships: [],
          priority: 0,
        };
      },
    }),
  ],
});

Dynamic framework routes require an explicit resource provider like this one. Agentize deliberately does not inspect arbitrary UI source code and guess which rendered text is authoritative.

Protected intranets

A protected Agentize interface uses one shared index for content that every admitted employee or service agent may read. The host application authenticates the complete /agents/* route family. Agentize does not manage accounts, roles, or document-level permissions.

Declare protected access and opt into intranet pages that use noindex to stay out of public search engines:

export default defineConfig({
  site: {
    name: "Example intranet",
    origin: "https://intranet.example",
    description: "Shared employee knowledge",
  },
  access: { mode: "protected" },
  sources: [
    markdown({
      root: "content/handbook",
      include: ["**/*.md"],
      includeNoindex: true,
    }),
  ],
});

Protected bundles fail closed. A framework integration must provide a host-owned request gate:

import { createAgentizeRouteHandlers } from "@nicolasakf/agentize/next";

const handlers = createAgentizeRouteHandlers({
  authorizeRequest(request) {
    return requireCompanyAccess(request);
  },
});

authorizeRequest runs before discovery, index, search, resource retrieval, and unknown Agentize paths. Return the host's 401 or 403 response to deny access, or return nothing to continue.

For a sidecar behind an authenticated reverse proxy, make the trust boundary explicit:

location ~ ^/agents(?:/|$) {
  auth_request /_company_auth;
  proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:4242;
}
agentize serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4242 --trust-upstream-protection

Use the trusted-upstream flag only when the proxy protects /agents and every path below it. Keep documents with narrower HR, finance, or team permissions out of this shared index.

Next.js

Run agentize init. It creates an App Router catch-all route under app/agents/[[...path]]/route.ts. The route uses the Node runtime because local query embedding and USearch require Node-compatible packages.

The adapter also exports withAgentize, which includes the generated bundle and native vector dependency in Next's server output:

import { withAgentize } from "@nicolasakf/agentize/next";

export default withAgentize({});

Build the Agentize bundle before the application build:

{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "agentize build && next build"
  }
}

命令

  • agentize init creates configuration and framework integration files.
  • agentize build produces an atomic .agentize/output/ bundle.
  • agentize dev watches sources, rebuilds, and serves on port 4242. Protected bundles require --trust-upstream-protection unless the runtime receives authorizeRequest programmatically.
  • agentize serve serves a generated bundle with the same protected-mode requirement.
  • agentize check validates resources, privacy exclusions, relationships, and Next.js route coverage.

协议

  • GET /agents discovers the site and its agent endpoints.
  • GET /agents/index lists semantic collections and paginated standalone resources.
  • POST /agents/search performs semantic-first retrieval, with optional filters on type, collection, tag, and language.
  • GET /agents/resources/:id returns JSON, or Markdown with Accept: text/markdown.

See the v0.2 protocol for request and response shapes. The v0.1 protocol remains available for older clients.

代理技巧

This repository ships two Agent Skills for coding agents. Install them with the open skills CLI:

npx skills add nicolasakf/agentize --all

Install one skill:

npx skills add nicolasakf/agentize --skill agentize-websites
npx skills add nicolasakf/agentize --skill search-agentized-websites
Skill 使用时
agentize-websites Installing, configuring, deploying, or troubleshooting Agentize in a website repository you control
search-agentized-websites Detecting and querying public or authenticated /agents/* endpoints without crawling HTML

Skills are maintained in .agents/skills/ and work with Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and 70+ other agents.

Privacy and deployment

Agentize indexes only declared sources. Admin, account, checkout, authentication, and internal API paths are excluded by default. Run agentize check in CI and review all warnings before deployment.

The generated bundle contains the full indexed text and embeddings. Treat a protected bundle as private application data and never publish it as a static asset. Protocol 0.2 targets self-hosted Node or Docker. Static and edge-only runtimes are not supported.

Every package is versioned together. Upgrading from 0.1 requires rebuilding the Agentize bundle before deployment.
